prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five frames, the camera wearer approaches a blue-framed glass facade with central sliding doors beneath an overhanging ceiling, moving from roughly 6–8 metres away in frame 1 to within 1 metre—within arm's reach of the door frame—by frame 5 as the doors slide open. In frame 1, two exterior potted plants flank the entrance at the far left (about 5 metres away) and partially cropped at the bottom-right corner (about 1.5–2 metres away), while the reflective glass wall appears as a uniform mid-grey plane that brightens progressively as the camera wearer walks straight toward it. Unlike the RGB image where outdoor palm reflections and indoor lighting create visual ambiguity, the depth map clearly reveals the exact moment the sliding doors part in frame 4 (as a narrow dark vertical slit) and open fully in frame 5 to expose the deeper interior lobby 3–10 metres beyond. Inside the open doorway in frame 5, silhouettes of a person in a white shirt at the right edge (about 3 metres away), a person in black standing left-of-centre (about 4.5 metres away, 1.5 metres behind the right person), a reception counter with flanked potted plants and an exit sign (4–6 metres away), and a distant person walking left (7–8 metres away) become dimly visible as darker grey shapes against the black background, all facing away from the camera wearer and toward the counter within arm's reach of the counter and nearby plants. However, the depth map is unreliable on the reflective glass in frames 1–4, rendering the panes as an opaque flat wall that completely occludes the indoor occupants visible through the glass in RGB, and it severely compresses depth contrast inside the lobby in frame 5.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates foreground objects and people against the building entrance as the camera wearer walks straight from roughly 7 metres out in frame 1 to the open doorway at 1 metre in frame 5, where the surrounding door frames come within the camera wearer's arm's reach. In frame 1, it detects the potted plant in a white geometric planter on the far left (about 5 metres away) as two stacked masks, while completely missing the partially cropped plant at the bottom right (1.5–2 metres away), and it detects one person visible through the glass doors; across frames 2–4, it tracks one to two people in front of the camera wearer who are either reflected in or seen through the closed glass panes at roughly 2–5 metres distance, including a reflection of the camera wearer and a companion walking forward within 1 metre of each other. By frame 5, once the sliding doors clear the view, the map segments four distinct people inside the lobby (3–8 metres ahead) plus a fifth false-positive 'person' mask (green) on the indoor potted plant between the man in black (pink mask, ~4.5 metres away, facing the counter away from the camera wearer) and the man in white partially cut off at the right door frame (brown mask, ~3 metres away, facing left and slightly away), along with a distant person walking left (cyan mask, ~7.5 metres away) and a person behind the reception desk (purple mask, ~6 metres away). Compared to the cluttered RGB reflections, the segmentation masks help isolate human figures across the approach, showing that the indoor people are within arm's reach of the counter, indoor plants, and each other on the right side. However, the map is unreliable because it confuses outdoor reflections on the glass with actual indoor people in frames 1–4, misses the reception counter, doors, and right-side plants, and misclassifies an indoor plant and background clutter as people in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, failing to detect any body or hand skeletons as the camera wearer walks from roughly 7 metres away in frame 1 to within 1 metre (arm's reach) of the opening sliding glass doors in frame 5. From the RGB strip, several people are present in the scene: reflections of the camera wearer and a nearby person walking toward the glass doors in frames 1–4 (appearing 2–5 metres away in front of the doorway), and four indoor occupants in frame 5 once the doors slide open—specifically a person in white on the right (~3 metres away, facing left/away), a person in black near the centre (~4.5 metres away, facing forward toward the reception desk and away from the camera wearer), a person walking away to the left (~7.5 metres away), and staff partially occluded behind the reception counter (~6 metres away, facing toward the lobby). In the RGB view, the indoor occupants near the counter and plants are within 1–2 metres and arm's reach of the counter, signage, and potted plants, while none of them look toward the camera wearer. Unlike a functioning skeleton map that would clarify limb positions and facing directions through glare, this pose map provides no spatial information beyond the RGB image and is entirely unreliable due to glass reflections and occlusion in frames 1–4 and the 3–8 metre distance and partial occlusions of the people inside the lobby in frame 5.
